newsitem.title: USA: Consumer prices move up 0.3 percent in February.
newsitem.headline: Consumer prices move up 0.3 percent in February.

text.p: Consumer prices moved up moderately in February, the Labour Department said Wednesday, new evidence supporting the view that inflation remains mostly under control.
The department said the Consumer Price Index rose 0.3 percent after expanding 0.1 percent in January.

With the often-volatile food and energy sector left out, the so-called core rate, which economists believe more closely follows underlying inflation trends, rose only 0.2 percent after being up 0.1 percent in January.
The February data was generally in line with Wall Street estimates that the overall and core rate would rise 0.2 percent.
The department said energy prices rose 0.3 percent after being up 0.8 percent in January, while food prices rose 0.3 percent after declining by the same amount in the prior month.

The consumer price data follows a report last week by the department showing wholesale prices dropped for the second consecutive month in February, showing no inflationary pressures whatsoever at that level.

These two pieces of information will likely be an important part of the discussion when Federal Reserve policy-makers meet in less than a week to consider monetary policy and the question of whether to raise interest rates to head off possible inflation.

Cheryl Katz, senior economist at Merrill Lynch and Co. Inc., said the index was "slightly worse than expected ... (but) all in all, today's number, I don't think, would make the Federal Reserve tighten."

The U.S. economy has nearly completed six years of expansion and while there have been few price pressures, there is some evidence that wage pressures are beginning to grow as a result of low unemployment levels.
Gasoline prices, which rose 0.7 percent in January, were unchanged last month, while home fuel oil prices registered a decline of 1.9 percent.
Food price increases were led by fresh vegetables, but this was partially offset by declines in some meat costs.
The department said transporation costs slipped 0.1 percent following a fall of 0.2 percent in January, while entertainment rose 0.2 percent. Airline fares were off 2.6 percent.
Housing prices rose 0.3 percent for the second month in a row while medical costs increased 0.2 percent.
